answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing a random, costly task whose result is checked against a public reference, with rewards released after a delay. The protocol caps how many tasks one account can claim at once and makes repeated claims require fresh escrow, so a sybil farm cannot multiply influence just by minting names. An attacker must fund many deposits and spend real effort producing valid work; failed or duplicated submissions lose escrow. A karst survey, walnut harvest, or cedar inventory could supply such a task.
